examples.solution_text:
(a) Use the same vertices for the row and column headings.
Record the roads $AB=19$, $AC=31$, $BC=43$, $BD=56$ and $CD=67$ in both directions.
There is no road between $A$ and $D$, and there are no loops.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} \text{From/To} & A & B & C & D \\ \hline A & - & 19 & 31 & - \\ B & 19 & - & 43 & 56 \\ C & 31 & 43 & - & 67 \\ D & - & 56 & 67 & - \end{array}$
(b) Each road connects the same two towns in both directions, so the matching entries are equal.

(a) Record each arrow in its starting vertex's row and finishing vertex's column.
From $A$, record $12$ to $B$ and $35$ to $C$.
From $B$, record $27$ to $A$ and $58$ to $D$.
From $C$, record $46$ to $B$.
From $D$, record $69$ to $C$.
Use dashes for all other entries.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} \text{From/To} & A & B & C & D \\ \hline A & - & 12 & 35 & - \\ B & 27 & - & - & 58 \\ C & - & 46 & - & - \\ D & - & - & 69 & - \end{array}$
(b) Opposite journeys are separate directed connections.
For example, $A\to B$ takes $12$ minutes but $B\to A$ takes $27$ minutes, so these matching entries are different.

examples.question_text:
Construct a directed network diagram from this table. The weights are journey times in minutes.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} \text{From/To} & P & Q & R & S \\ \hline P & - & 14 & 23 & - \\ Q & 36 & - & - & 47 \\ R & - & 58 & - & - \\ S & - & - & 69 & - \end{array}$

methods.description: Use vertex headings for rows and columns; record each direct edge weight in both matching cells and use the stated no-connection convention elsewhere. Read individual or missing entries by the same method.

methods.description: Record each arrow's weight in the starting vertex's row and finishing vertex's column; treat reverse arrows separately and use the stated no-connection convention elsewhere.

methods.description: Draw one vertex per heading, then read each row and draw a weighted arrow to the column vertex for every connection. Omit entries denoting no connection.
